description: Add the missing head resources: preconnect hints for the Google Fonts origins, an apple-touch-icon, a web app manifest with 192px and 512px PNG icons, og:image:type, and twitter:image:alt. Also delete the unreferenced public/vite.svg template leftover.

New: public/site.webmanifest, public/apple-touch-icon.png (180), public/icon-192.png, public/icon-512.png, scripts/generate-icons.mjs, scripts/icons.manifest.json. Deleted public/vite.svg. THE ICONS ARE NOT HAND-EXPORTED — step 2 says 'generate', so scripts/generate-icons.mjs rasterizes public/dilsher2.svg and is wired into the build (node scripts/generate-icons.mjs && ...) plus exposed as `yarn generate:icons`, following exactly the conventions PERF-001 established for optimize-images.mjs: outputs COMMITTED, skip via a sha256 of the source bytes + render settings (not mtimes), and graceful degradation when sharp is unavailable. BOTH degradation branches were exercised for real by hiding node_modules/sharp: outputs present -> warning + exit 0; an output missing -> clear error + exit 1. Its hash manifest lives at scripts/icons.manifest.json and deliberately NOT in public/, which Vite copies verbatim into dist/ — build state must not be deployed. THE SOURCE SVG COULD NOT BE USED AS-IS AND THIS IS THE ONE REAL DESIGN DECISION HERE: dilsher2.svg is a solid BLACK disc with the DS monogram knocked out as transparency, so rasterized directly it is a black-on-transparent icon — invisible on the site's own dark theme, and iOS ignores transparency and composites apple-touch-icon onto an opaque backdrop. The disc is therefore tinted to #f5f5f5 (neutral-100, the site's heading colour) via a dest-in composite that preserves the knockout and its anti-aliasing, then laid over an opaque #0a0a0a (neutral-950, matching theme_color/background_color), so the backdrop shows through the letterforms. MEASURED, not assumed: all 3 PNGs report channels=3 / hasAlpha=false / min alpha 255 (fully opaque, iOS-safe), and mark-vs-ground contrast is 18.16:1. GEOMETRY: the SVG's own viewBox padding leaves the mark at only 57% of the canvas, which reads as lost in a launcher tile, so it is trimmed out of that padding and re-inset to MARK_RATIO 0.72 — measured back at 72.2/71.9/72.1% and centred to within 0.1%. Staying under 80% is what keeps it inside the maskable safe zone, which is why site.webmanifest can honestly declare purpose 'any maskable' on both icons rather than the usual unverified copy-paste. Verified: yarn lint passes; yarn build passes (only the documented fetchPriority SSR warning); step 6 `grep -r 'vite.svg' index.html src/ | wc -l` = 0; step 7 all 3 PNGs + site.webmanifest appear in dist/ and are byte-identical to public/ (cmp clean), and dist/vite.svg does not exist; step 8 the manifest JSON.parse's in both public/ and dist/. Also served dist/ on vite preview and curled the new URLs: apple-touch-icon 200 image/png, icon-192 200 image/png, icon-512 200 image/png, site.webmanifest 200 application/manifest+json. NOTE /vite.svg also returns 200 there — that is vite preview's SPA fallback serving index.html (POLISH-001 documented this), NOT a surviving file; dist/vite.svg genuinely does not exist. PNG output is byte-identical across a full regenerate on this platform, so the committed icons will not churn; cross-platform determinism was NOT testable here, so if a future loop sees spurious icon diffs after a platform switch, that is why. PERF-003 IS NOW UNBLOCKED: its step 1 wanted these preconnect hints. They are already useful today even though the font is still an @import in src/index.css — the connection warms while that stylesheet is being fetched and parsed — and PERF-003 should move the request to <link> tags right beside them.

description: Fix the project card aria-label that hides all card content from screen readers. In src/components/Projects.jsx an <a> wraps the entire card and carries aria-label="View details about the project {title}". Because aria-label on a link overrides its subtree's accessible name, screen reader users hear only that label and lose the h3, the description paragraph, and every technology chip. The label is also factually wrong: the href points to the live external site, not a details page.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the vite dev server on localhost:3000. Took PRD step 1's aria-labelledby option rather than deleting the label outright: the <a> wraps the ENTIRE card, so with no label at all the computed name becomes the whole subtree concatenated ('Screenshot of the project X X <150-word description> TypeScript Node.js ... View Project') — technically compliant but a worse announcement. Each card now has aria-labelledby={`project-title-N project-new-tab-N`}, pointing at the existing h3 (now id'd) and a new sr-only span '(opens in a new tab)' placed beside the visible 'View Project' CTA. The new-tab hint lives in its own span rather than inside the h3 so the heading's own accessible name stays exactly the project title in the heading rotor. VERIFIED IN CHROME'S REAL A11Y TREE (not just my own accname replication): the three links compute to 'Dualmint Marketplace (opens in a new tab)', 'Ipseity Network (opens in a new tab)', 'Real-Time Collaborative Editor (opens in a new tab)'; Playwright's own getByRole resolution independently reported the same three names. Description paragraphs and all 15 technology chips remain as separate nodes in the a11y tree under each link, none inside an aria-hidden subtree; 0 duplicate ids and 0 dangling idref on the page; target=_blank and rel=noopener noreferrer intact on all 3 cards plus the 'All Projects' link. No visual change: the sr-only span computes to position absolute / 1x1 / clip rect(0,0,0,0) on all 3 cards, screenshots show the CTA row unchanged, no horizontal overflow at 780px or 375px, hover still applies rgba(147,51,234,0.6) to the card border, and the link is still focusable and focus lands on it. yarn lint passes, yarn build passes, and the old label string appears 0 times in src/ AND 0 times in the built bundle. CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM'S PREMISE, worth knowing for A11Y-005/006: the claim that screen reader users 'lose the h3, the description paragraph, and every technology chip' was overstated for the raw a11y tree — a BEFORE snapshot showed Chrome still exposed the h3, paragraph and chips as descendants even with the aria-label present. What was genuinely broken is the announced accessible NAME (wrong text, and the only thing many SRs read when the link is focused or listed in the links rotor), and that it falsely promised a details page. The fix is still correct; the severity framing was just sharper than the tree warranted.

description: Fix the five WCAG AA color contrast failures. text-neutral-500 (#737373) on the bg-neutral-950 (#0a0a0a) page background measures 4.18:1, and 3.78:1 where it sits on bg-neutral-900 cards. Both fall short of the 4.5:1 minimum for normal-size text. Changing to text-neutral-400 (#a3a3a3) yields 7.85:1 and passes comfortably with a barely perceptible visual change.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the vite dev server on localhost:3000. All five text locations moved to text-neutral-400; `grep -rc text-neutral-500 src/` totals exactly 1 (the 36px 'Me' in About.jsx, deliberately kept per step 2). border-neutral-800 -> border-neutral-700 in Hero/About/Technologies(x2)/Projects, leaving 0 occurrences of border-neutral-800; email underline purple-400/40 -> /70. All five borders confirmed rgb(64,64,64) and the underline rgba(192,132,252,0.7) in the browser. AXE RESULT: 0 color-contrast violations, 86 passes. >>> BUT STEP 6 HAD TO BE RUN WITH A TEST-ONLY WORKAROUND, READ THIS <<< Run straight, axe reports 86 color-contrast VIOLATIONS that are all false positives: it resolves the page background to #ffffff and reports the light text as failing against white. Cause: html and body are both rgba(0,0,0,0) and the dark ground is painted only by the fixed z-[-1] div in src/App.jsx:13, which a contrast algorithm cannot attribute as an element's background. That is exactly the defect POLISH-001 step 2 owns. To get a real measurement I set document.body.style.backgroundColor='#0a0a0a' at test time only (source untouched); axe then returned 0 violations / 86 passes. ONCE POLISH-001 LANDS, AXE WILL PASS NATIVELY AND THIS WORKAROUND CAN BE DROPPED — until then any axe run on this page reports garbage contrast numbers, so do not trust a raw axe scan here. A further 30 nodes come back 'incomplete' (background gradient) covering Hero, About and the Technologies heading, including the four About dt labels this item changed, so axe could not confirm those. Verified them empirically instead: hid all content except the painter div, screenshotted, and scanned every pixel for the brightest background on the page — rgb(35,35,53) at the top centre. Against that true worst case, neutral-400 measures 6.11:1 on the page and 6.54:1 on the card fill (both need 4.5), neutral-300 body copy 10.39:1, and purple-400 links 5.83:1. The OLD neutral-500 measures 3.25:1 there, so the defect was real and somewhat worse than this item's flat-background estimate of 4.18:1. The kept 'Me' at 36px needs only 3:1 and measures 3.25:1 — it passes, but the margin is thinner than the 4.18 figure implied, so do not reuse neutral-500 for anything smaller. >>> STEP 4 DOES NOT ACHIEVE WHAT IT CLAIMS — IMPLEMENTED AS SPECIFIED, BUT THE PREMISE IS WRONG <<< border-neutral-700 measures 1.91:1 against #0a0a0a and 1.49:1 at the gradient peak, NOT the 3:1 that WCAG 1.4.11 requires; the step's own reasoning does not hold. (border-neutral-800 was 1.31:1, so this is still a real ~46% improvement in delineation, just not a conformance fix.) Reaching 3:1 needs about neutral-500 (4.18:1 flat / 3.25:1 at peak) — neutral-600 only reaches 2.53:1 — which is a much more visible design change than 'barely perceptible', so it is the user's call and was NOT taken unilaterally. Also worth knowing: the cards are not delineated by the border alone as the step assumes; they carry bg-neutral-900/40, though that fill is only 1.03:1 against the page so it contributes almost nothing. Whether 1.4.11 even applies is arguable, since these are decorative borders around static content rather than UI component boundaries. STEP 7 CANNOT BE DONE FROM HERE: WAVE runs against a deployed URL and these changes are not deployed. Also confirmed: no horizontal overflow at 375px, all 30 reveals still reach opacity 1, the GithubContributions error state was exercised for real (by temporarily moving public/github-contributions.json aside, then restored byte-identical) and renders at rgb(163,163,163); the loading state shares an identical class string and is covered by the same edit but was not separately forced. yarn lint and yarn build both pass.

description: Add a global :focus-visible style. No element in the codebase suppresses outlines, so default browser rings are intact, but only one element (the navbar section links) has an authored focus style and it is a color change with no ring. On a #0a0a0a background the default ring is nearly invisible in some browsers. A single global rule covers all 15 interactive elements at once.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the vite dev server on localhost:3000. src/index.css gained a `:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c084fc; outline-offset: 2px }` rule inside @layer base, so a Tailwind utility can still override it per-element if ever needed. Verified in the built CSS too: `:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #c084fc;outline-offset:2px}` is present in dist/assets/index-*.css. Item premises both confirmed before starting: `grep -rc outline-none src/ index.html` = 0 (nothing suppresses outlines) and exactly ONE authored focus style existed (Navbar's colour-only focus-visible:text-purple-400, which is additive and was left in place). >>> THE GLOBAL RULE ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH — A CONTAINER WAS CLIPPING THE RING, AND FIXING IT REQUIRED A SECOND EDIT <<< The navbar's <ul> carries overflow-x-auto, which makes it a scroll container that CLIPS its children. The ring (2px wide + 2px offset = 4px outside the link box) was cut top and bottom by exactly 2px each, so the 5 nav links rendered with ONLY their left and right bars — visually confirmed in a zoomed screenshot, not just measured. The first and last links additionally lost their outer bar, having no horizontal room. Fixed on the <ul> with `p-1 -m-1 scroll-p-1`: p-1 gives the clip box the 4px the ring needs on all four sides, -m-1 cancels it so navbar layout is unchanged (header height stays 57px at 1280 and 118px at 375, measured before and after), and scroll-p-1 keeps that room in view when tabbing scrolls a link horizontally. AFTER the fix, a full Tab sweep at 1280x800, 780x493 and 375x700 reports every stop at outline-width 2px / style solid / color rgb(192,132,252) / offset 2px, with a generic ancestor-walk clipping check (any ancestor whose overflow is not visible) returning 0 clipped rings at 1280 and 780. CONTRAST MEASURED FROM RENDERED PIXELS, not assumed: screenshotted focused elements, classified ring-core pixels, excluded anti-aliased blend pixels, and sampled the real painted background adjacent to the ring. Ring vs page background rgb(10,10,10) = 7.49:1 (exactly matching this item's estimate), vs the bg-neutral-900/40 card fill rgb(15,15,15) = 7.25:1, vs the navbar/gradient area rgb(17,17,22) = 7.12:1. All far above the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 floor, so step 5 passes on both backgrounds. STEP 3 COUNT CORRECTION: the item says '15 interactive elements'; there are 19 tab stops at 1280x800 and 20 at narrow widths. The 20th is NOT an authored control — it is the GitHub heatmap's overflow-x-auto wrapper div, which Chrome makes implicitly keyboard-focusable so the container can be scrolled by keyboard. That is correct behaviour and it now gets a visible ring too. STEP 4: focus is never trapped (tabbing past the last control returns to browser UI / body, verified by the sweep terminating) and no stop lands off the top of the viewport or under the header. ONE PRE-EXISTING CAVEAT, NOT INTRODUCED HERE: at 375px the nav list overflows its container, and Chrome does not scroll that nested horizontal container when focus enters it (ulScrollLeft stays 0), so the last link 'Contact' sits 11px past the container edge and its ring is cut on the right. Measured with the pre-change class list restored at runtime, the nav ALREADY overflowed by 7px at 375px, i.e. that link's own TEXT was already clipped before this item — the ring inherits an existing nav-layout problem rather than causing one. Forcing the container to its scroll end makes the ring fit exactly (0.1px overhang), so the room is there; only Chrome's focus-scroll of the nested container is missing. Fixing it properly means changing how the nav sizes or wraps at narrow widths, which is a design decision and was not taken unilaterally. MOUSE BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED: clicking a link paints no ring — in this browser the anchor is not even focused on click, and :focus-visible would not match anyway — so the visual design is unchanged for pointer users while keyboard users get the ring. yarn lint passes, yarn build passes (the only build warning is the pre-existing, documented fetchPriority SSR warning that RENDER-002 says not to 'fix').

description: Optimize the image payload, which is the single largest performance problem in the repo: roughly 4.5MB of images are shipped to render three 200px-wide thumbnails and one 384px avatar. Two files are PNG data misnamed with a .jpg extension (project-1.jpg is 2.2MB at 1900x1318; project-3.jpg is 2245x1324), dilsherSinghProfile.png is a 1.2MB photo stored as PNG at 1024x1024, and project-2.png is 922KB at 2553x1308. Vite copies all of them into dist byte-for-byte with zero optimization.
notes: Complete and verified 2026-08-12. dist/assets went 4.5MB -> 288KB; the four images total 78KB, down from 4.4MB. STRUCTURE: full-resolution sources moved to src/assets/originals/ with extensions corrected to match their real encoding (project-1.jpg and project-3.jpg were PNG data — confirmed by magic bytes — and are now project-1.png / project-3.png). Nothing imports src/assets/originals/, so Vite never bundles it; it is the pipeline's input only. Generated WebP lives in src/assets/optimized/ and IS committed, so a build still succeeds on a host where sharp's platform binary is unusable. src/assets/projects/ no longer exists. Deleted the unreferenced src/assets/dilsherSinghProfile.jpg (174KB). PIPELINE: scripts/optimize-images.mjs (new) uses sharp 0.35.3 (added as a devDependency via yarn, so yarn.lock stays in yarn-v1 format) and is wired into the build as `node scripts/optimize-images.mjs && node --env-file-if-exists=.env scripts/fetch-github.mjs && vite build`; also exposed as `yarn optimize:images`. Widths are ~2x display size: profile 1024x1024 -> 768x768 (57.8KB), projects -> 400px wide (9.9KB / 5.7KB / 4.2KB). Re-encode is skipped via a sha256 of the source bytes plus the encode settings, recorded in src/assets/optimized/.manifest.json — content-hashed rather than mtime-based because a git checkout does not preserve mtimes. VERIFIED: yarn lint passes; yarn build passes; `du -sk dist/assets` = 288 (target <500); `find dist/assets -type f \( -name '*.webp' -o -name '*.png' -o -name '*.jpg' \) -size +150k | wc -l` = 0; re-running the script is a no-op ('4 images already up to date'); both degradation paths were exercised by hiding node_modules/sharp — outputs present gives a warning and exit 0, an output missing gives a clear error and exit 1. IMAGE 404 CHECK: Playwright could not run in this sandbox (missing browser system libraries), so instead every image URL referenced by the built bundle was extracted from dist/assets/*.js and curled against the vite preview on :3000 — all 4 returned 200 with content-type image/webp, and the only other image (the 1.9KB navbar logo) is inlined as a base64 data URI by Vite so it cannot 404. description: Stop delaying the largest contentful paint with entry animations. In src/components/Hero.jsx the LCP image is held at opacity 0 with a 1.2 second animation delay and the bio paragraph is delayed 1 second. This deliberately defers the LCP element by over a second and by itself caps the Lighthouse performance score regardless of any other optimization.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against `vite preview` on localhost:3000 (the BUILT bundle, per steps 4-7), measured before/after with a git worktree of HEAD served on :3001. HEADLINE RESULT: real observed LCP went 2356/2362/2314ms -> 368/156/137ms across three matched Lighthouse runs, and LCP now equals FCP exactly in every run, i.e. the largest paint IS the first paint. THE HERO IMAGE IS NO LONGER WRAPPED IN A Reveal AT ALL — that is the core of the fix and a deliberate deviation from a literal reading of step 1, which only asked to reduce its delay. Any opacity animation on the LCP element defers it regardless of delay, because Chrome does not record an opacity-transitioning element as painted until the transition ENDS (measured: each element's LCP entry lands at FCP + its own delay + its own duration). Rendering the image plainly makes it paint on the first frame independent of hydration; it now carries fetchPriority="high" alongside the existing width/height/loading=eager. Verified by sampling computed opacity every frame from an addInitScript BEFORE navigation: the image exists at 122ms and is opacity 1 on the very first frame it exists, 0 of 67 samples below 1. The four above-the-fold hero TEXT reveals keep their animation but were cut from delays 0/0.5/0.75/1.0 at 0.5s duration to delays 0/0.05/0.1/0.15 at a shared HERO_DURATION of 0.3s, since on narrow viewports the avatar drops below the fold and the h1/bio become the LCP candidates (measured at 375px: LCP 904ms -> 592ms). Whole hero now settles in 0.45s vs 1.7s. Below-the-fold reveals were left at the 0.5s default. STEP 3: width/height added to all 3 Projects.jsx images and the Navbar logo (562x106); all 5 images on the page now have both attributes and every attribute ratio matches its natural ratio exactly. The project dimensions are NOT hardcoded — scripts/optimize-images.mjs now emits src/assets/optimized/dimensions.json (committed, imported by src/constants/index.js as project.imageSize) so a change to the pipeline's target width can never leave a stale aspect ratio in the markup; the manifest values became {key,width,height} to carry them, which re-encoded all four images once to byte-IDENTICAL output. HONEST CAVEAT ON CLS: 0 before and 0 after, with zero layout-shift entries even scrolling the full page at 400kbps. The width/height attributes do demonstrably reserve the box (the project images report complete:false with their final height already correct), but I could not produce a measurable shift in the baseline to fix — Chrome's lazy-load threshold fetches those images well before they enter the viewport, and off-screen shifts do not count toward CLS. Step 3 is correct defensive practice, not a measured win. STEP 7 CAVEAT WORTH READING: Lighthouse mobile scored 99/99/99 (median 99, target 95) — but the BASELINE also scored 99/99/99 with the same simulated LCP of 2.1s. Lighthouse's simulated (Lantern) throttling models network and CPU critical paths and is BLIND to CSS transition wall-clock time, so it did not detect this defect at all; only the observed metric did. Do not use the simulated Lighthouse score to validate animation-related LCP work. Also confirmed: RENDER-001's guarantees still hold (reducedMotion 'reduce' -> all 30 reveals at opacity 1 / transform none, hero image opacity 1), the entry animation still visibly plays for normal visitors (partial opacity and offset both observed on the h1, settling at opacity 1 / transform none), reveal count 31 -> 30 confirming exactly one Reveal removed, yarn lint passes, yarn build passes, and the only console error is the pre-existing sandbox-firewall cert failure on fonts.googleapis.com. NOT DONE, OWNED ELSEWHERE: Lighthouse still flags render-blocking-resources (~450ms) and prioritize-lcp-image (~300ms, wants a preload hint) — both are the Google Fonts @import and head-resource work that PERF-003 and SEO-003 own; uses-responsive-images wants a srcset, which no PRD item currently covers.

description: Fix the render-blocking font load and add caching headers. The Inter font is pulled in via a CSS @import at the top of src/index.css, which is the slowest possible path: the browser must download and parse index.css before it even discovers the font CSS URL, then fetch that, then the font files. The request also asks for the full 100-900 weight range in both roman and italic, but the site uses no italics. Separately there is no vercel.json, so hash-named immutable assets are served with max-age=0.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against `vite preview` on localhost:3000 (the BUILT, prerendered bundle). THREE FILES: index.html (the font <link> moved here, beside SEO-003's preconnects), src/index.css (@import deleted), vercel.json (new). Final URL: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:opsz,wght@14..32,100..900&display=swap >>> THE CORE MECHANISM WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED <<< Built HEAD (a16abf6) in a git worktree and served it on :3001 alongside the new build on :3000, then compared PerformanceResourceTiming for the fonts.googleapis.com request. Its initiatorType flips from 'css' to 'link', which is categorical rather than noise: BASELINE discovered the font at 59.5ms, 2.8ms AFTER the app stylesheet had finished downloading (responseEnd 56.7) — a serial chain; AFTER discovers it at 59.1ms, 1.0ms BEFORE the app stylesheet is even requested (60.1) — parallel, found by the preload scanner in the initial HTML. Reproduced on a second matched pair (baseline 68.0 vs responseEnd 63.2 = serial; after 52.0 vs 52.3 = parallel). PAYLOAD, measured with curl rather than estimated: the old ital+opsz+wght request returns 4,774 bytes of CSS and 14 @font-face rules; roman-only returns 2,379 bytes and 7 rules, i.e. half. >>> DELIBERATE DEVIATION ON STEP 2, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT DROVE IT <<< The site uses exactly five weights — 100 font-thin (Hero h1), 300 font-light, 400 default, 500 font-medium, 600 font-semibold — with no strong/b/em anywhere and Contact.jsx explicitly not-italic, so dropping the slanted axis is unambiguously safe. But narrowing wght@100..900 to 100..600 saves EXACTLY ZERO BYTES: Google returns the IDENTICAL font file for both (same URL, UcCo3FwrK3iLTcviYwY.woff2, 72,920 bytes latin), changing only the declared font-weight descriptor. It would, however, make any future request for weight 700 clamp silently to 600. Zero benefit against a real silent-regression footgun, so the full range stays and only the ital axis was dropped. Also measured and rejected: discrete weights (wght@100;300;400;500;600) are much WORSE — 35 @font-face rules, 12,354 bytes of CSS, and five separate font files instead of one. >>> A REAL 24.7KB WIN LEFT ON THE TABLE ON PURPOSE — USER'S CALL <<< Dropping the opsz axis too (family=Inter:wght@100..600) makes Google serve a genuinely different, smaller file: latin woff2 48,256 bytes vs 72,920, a 24,664-byte / 33.8% cut on the critical path. Not taken because it pins Inter's optical size and is a site-wide typography change — the h1 is text-8xl and optical sizing is exactly what that axis is for. Worth deciding deliberately; it is the largest remaining font win. >>> STEP 9 IS NOT ACHIEVABLE VIA STEP 1'S APPROACH. READ BEFORE RE-OPENING THIS ITEM. <<< A cross-origin <link rel="stylesheet"> is render-blocking BY DEFINITION, so Lighthouse's 'Eliminate render-blocking resources' audit will still list the font stylesheet in production. Moving it out of the @import removes one serial round trip from the DISCOVERY chain (measured above) but does not make the resource non-blocking, and step 1 mandates the <link>. The two ways to actually clear step 9: (a) load it async via media="print" onload="this.media='all'" with a <noscript> fallback — costs a JS dependency and a guaranteed extra style recalc; (b) SELF-HOST the font, which removes the third-party origin altogether, is the best answer for both performance and privacy, but needs committed woff2 files plus a build step and would make SEO-003's two preconnect hints dead code. Neither is in this item's steps and both are judgement calls, so neither was taken unilaterally. description: Split the JavaScript bundle. The production build emits a single 335KB chunk (112KB gzipped) containing React, framer-motion, and react-icons alongside all application code, so any source change invalidates the entire cached bundle for returning visitors.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against `vite preview` on localhost:3000 (the BUILT, prerendered bundle). Step 4 asks that total gzip 'not increase relative to the current 112KB baseline', which would pass trivially against a stale number, so I measured the REAL before/after: 63,822 -> 63,920 bytes, +98 bytes (+0.15%), which is the expected per-chunk framing overhead and is comfortably 'not meaningful'. (b) Step 3 ('no chunk exceeds 150KB raw') was FAILING BEFORE THIS ITEM at 188.24 kB — splitting is what fixes it, not a property that was already true. It now passes with react-vendor at 141.80 kB, but note that is only ~8KB of headroom; a React 19 upgrade could breach it, and the fix would be to split react-dom from react rather than to raise the ceiling. >>> STEP 1 NAMES A framer-motion CHUNK THAT CANNOT EXIST, AND RESOLVING THAT IS THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL HERE <<< framer-motion has not been imported since RENDER-001 replaced it with the CSS-based Reveal component; `grep -rn framer-motion src/ index.html scripts/` returns 4 hits and ALL FOUR ARE COMMENTS (src/index.css:99, src/components/Reveal.jsx:9/34/78). It was in package.json as a 3.7MB dependency that Rollup never saw, so a manualChunks entry for it would emit nothing. RENDER-001's notes explicitly left this decision to PERF-004, so I removed the dependency with `yarn remove framer-motion` (yarn, NOT npm — see the npm-rewrites-yarn.lock warning in the PERF-001 log). The lockfile diff is exactly 7 deleted lines, the framer-motion entry alone; tslib stays because another package still needs it. ZERO bundle impact, and that was verified rather than assumed: all three chunk hashes are byte-identical before and after the removal, which is itself the proof it was never bundled. Beware one false positive if you re-check this — `grep -i framer dist/assets/*.js` MATCHES, but the hit is `unstable_forceFrameRate` ('FrameR') in React's scheduler, not framer-motion. THE SPLIT IS MATCHED ON PATH SEGMENTS (`/node_modules/<pkg>/`), not bare substrings, so a package merely containing one of these names cannot be swept into the wrong chunk; react-dom/react/scheduler deliberately SHARE one chunk because react-dom imports scheduler and separating them would create a cross-chunk cycle. THE SSR BUILD IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNSPLIT via the `isSsrBuild` guard in the config callback: dist/server is a build intermediate that scripts/prerender.mjs imports once and then deletes, so chunking it would add module-resolution work for no caching benefit. Confirmed dist/server/entry-server.js is still a single 36.90 kB file and the prerender still injects 56,540 characters — byte-for-byte the same figure A11Y-006 recorded, i.e. the static HTML is completely unaffected. >>> THE ACTUAL POINT OF THIS ITEM WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED <<< Step 2-4 only count files and bytes; they never test the caching claim. I rebuilt after a real source edit (a class-string change in App.jsx, since an added COMMENT is stripped by minification and produces byte-identical output — my first attempt at this proved nothing and looked like a pass) and confirmed only index-Bkvt-VHm.js -> index-DErpGQli.js rotated, while react-vendor-DJwEGQ5P.js and icons-vendor-6OzOH3Cg.js kept identical hashes. So a returning visitor now re-downloads 9.50 kB gzip per deploy instead of 63.82 kB — an 85% reduction. App.jsx was restored and `git diff src/` is empty. Vite emits modulepreload hints for BOTH vendor chunks, so the split adds no request waterfall — verified in dist/index.html. yarn lint passes; yarn build passes (only the documented fetchPriority SSR warning). Only console error is the pre-existing fonts.googleapis.com cert failure from the sandbox firewall. MEASUREMENT NOTE: this run's viewport was 780x493, so docHeight reads 6605 and the projects scroll 4002, versus the 5435/3263 earlier loops recorded at 1280x800. That is the viewport, not a regression — JS chunking cannot move layout.

description: Make entry animations degrade to visible content, and honor prefers-reduced-motion. This is a hard prerequisite for RENDER-002: every whileInView animation sets initial={{ opacity: 0 }} as an inline style, so prerendering the app as-is would emit HTML whose text is present but invisible, which search engines may discount and which would defeat the purpose of prerendering. Additionally none of the 7 animating components honors prefers-reduced-motion; because framer-motion writes inline styles, a CSS media query cannot override it and the fix must happen in JS.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12. All 31 entry animations across Hero, About, Technologies, Experience, Projects, GithubContributions and Contact were converted from framer-motion to a new src/components/Reveal.jsx (IntersectionObserver + CSS classes) plus a `.reveal` block in src/index.css. The base state is now VISIBLE: hiding only applies under `.js .reveal` inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), and the `js` class is added by a synchronous inline script in index.html <head>. So content is visible for crawlers, for JS-off visitors, and under reduced motion, and there is no visible-then-hidden flash once RENDER-002 prerenders. DEVIATION FROM STEP 1: <MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"> was deliberately NOT added. Converting every animation left zero framer-motion imports in src/, so MotionConfig would have had nothing to configure. Reduced motion is instead handled by the CSS media query, which is strictly stronger — it applies before hydration and with JS disabled, neither of which MotionConfig can do. framer-motion is still listed in package.json but is now unused; removing it was left out of scope (note PERF-004 references it as a vendor chunk). Side effect: main JS chunk 299KB -> 187KB (gzip 100KB -> 63.5KB). Browser-verified on the built preview at localhost:3000 with Playwright: reducedMotion 'reduce' -> all 31 reveals at opacity 1 / transform none immediately and before any is-visible class is applied; default motion -> below-fold elements correctly staged at opacity 0 translateY(-40px) then transition in on scroll, and a full viewport-by-viewport scroll pass revealed 31/31 with 0 stranded; javaScriptEnabled:false against a prerender stand-in (client DOM baked into dist/index.html with the module script stripped) -> all 7 headings visible, hero bio visible, 0 of 31 reveals hidden, and 0 occurrences of inline 'opacity:0' in that 107KB static HTML, which pre-validates RENDER-002's final assertion; 0 console errors/warnings; no horizontal overflow at 375px despite the translateX offsets. Step 7's dist/index.html grep still cannot be run for real until RENDER-002 lands. UPDATE 2026-08-12, RENDER-002 has now landed and step 7 was run for real against the prerendered dist/index.html: `grep -o 'opacity:0' dist/index.html | wc -l` outputs 0, and a JS-disabled load of the genuinely prerendered page shows all 7 headings at opacity 1 with 0 of 30 reveals hidden. This item's design held up under prerendering with no changes, including no flash of visible-then-hidden content.

Separately, the dark background is painted by a fixed div with z-[-1] in src/App.jsx rather than on the body, so overscroll and rubber-band areas flash white, and the negative z-index would break if any ancestor ever creates a stacking context.
notes: Complete and browser-verified 2026-08-12 against the BUILT dist/. Two changes only: src/index.css gained `@layer base { body { @apply bg-neutral-950 } } ` (emits body{background-color:rgb(10 10 10)}), and public/404.html is new. >>> THE HEADLINE RESULT IS THAT AXE NOW MEASURES THIS PAGE HONESTLY, WHICH IS WHAT A11Y-002 PREDICTED AND WHAT A11Y-004/005/006 WERE WAITING ON <<< A full color-contrast scan with NO test-time workaround (verified: document.body inline style attribute is null) returns 0 violations / 98 passes / 19 incomplete, against the previous 86 FALSE-POSITIVE violations raw, or 86 passes only with the body background faked at runtime. The residual 19 are the radial gradient ('background color could not be determined due to a background gradient') plus 'content too short'; that gradient still lives on the fixed painter div and no body rule can fix it, so those will stay incomplete. A full all-rules axe scan is also 0 violations. The fixed painter div only ever covers the viewport, which is why that area used to flash white.
